quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 102B Paternity leave

facts.prompt: When can paternity leave be taken?
facts.tip: Up to 10 days before, or within three months after, the date of delivery.

quote.text: the leave will be granted for a period up to 10 days before or within three months after the date of delivery.

facts.prompt: What is hospital leave leave salary?
facts.tip: Earned leave salary for the first 120 days, then half pay leave salary.

quote.text: equal to leave salary while on earned leave, for the first 120 days of any period of such leave; and (2) equal to leave salary during half pay leave, for the remaining period of any such leave.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 104 Hospital leave salary

facts.prompt: Is hospital leave debited to the leave account?
facts.tip: No, and it may be combined with any other admissible leave.

quote.text: Hospital leave is not debited against the leave account and may be combined with any other leave which may be admissible.

facts.prompt: Can leave be retrospectively commuted into another kind?
facts.tip: Yes, into any other kind admissible when the original leave was granted. Earned leave cannot be commuted, with a stated exception.

quote.text: Any leave granted under these rules may be retrospectively commuted into any other kind of leave admissible to the officer at the time the original leave was granted
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 76 Retrospective commutation

facts.prompt: What is the time limit for retrospective commutation of leave?
facts.tip: No commutation of leave is allowed after one year from the date of sanction of leave.

quote.text: no commutation of leave shall be permitted on expiry of one year from the date of sanction of leave.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 76 second proviso / Rule 89(i)

facts.prompt: Can an officer claim retrospective commutation as a right?
facts.tip: No. The granting authority may commute it, but the officer cannot claim it as a matter of right.

quote.text: The authority which granted leave to an officer can commute it retrospectively into leave of a different kind which may be admissible but the officer concerned cannot claim it as a matter of right
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 89(i) Commutation with retrospective effect

facts.prompt: What follows automatically when leave is commuted into another kind?
facts.tip: Arrears of leave salary are drawn, or amounts overdrawn are recovered.

quote.text: Commutation of one kind of leave into another automatically carries with it the drawal of arrears of leave salary or recovery of amounts overdrawn.

facts.prompt: What does 'ordinary leave' include?
facts.tip: Ordinary leave means earned leave, half-pay leave, commuted leave, leave not due and leave without allowances.

quote.text: ‘Ordinary leave’ includes earned leave, half-pay leave, commuted leave, leave not due and leave without allowances.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 77(i) Ordinary leave

facts.prompt: What does 'special leave' include?
facts.tip: Special leave includes disability leave, maternity leave, paternity leave, child adoption leave and hospital leave.

quote.text: ‘Special leave’ includes disability leave, maternity leave, *paternity leave, †child adoption leave and hospital leave.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 77(ii) Special leave

facts.prompt: What is 'half-pay leave' earned in respect of?
facts.tip: Half-pay leave is leave earned in respect of completed years of service.

quote.text: ‘Half-pay leave’ means leave earned in respect of completed years of service.

facts.prompt: Who is an 'officer in permanent employ'?
facts.tip: One who holds a permanent post substantively, or holds a lien (or would hold it but for suspension) on a permanent post.

quote.text: ‘Officer in permanent employ’ means an officer who holds substantively a permanent post or who holds a lien on a permanent post or who would hold a lien on a permanent post had the lien not been suspended.

facts.prompt: How many days of half-pay leave per completed year of service?
facts.tip: 20 days for each completed year of service.

quote.text: The half-pay leave admissible to an officer in permanent employ in respect of each completed year of service is 20 days.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 83 Half-pay leave

facts.prompt: For what reasons can half-pay leave be availed?
facts.tip: On private affairs or on medical certificate.

quote.text: Half-pay leave as provided in Rule 83 may be availed of on private affairs or on medical certificate.

facts.prompt: How much commuted leave can be granted?
facts.tip: Not more than half the half-pay leave due.

quote.text: Commuted leave not exceeding half the amount of half-pay leave due may be granted to an officer in permanent employ.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 84 Commuted leave

facts.prompt: How much half-pay leave is debited when commuted leave is granted?
facts.tip: Twice the commuted leave is debited against half-pay leave due.

quote.text: When Commuted Leave is granted twice the amount of such leave shall be debited against the half-pay leave due.

facts.prompt: What minimum service is needed for leave for superior qualifications under Rule 91?
facts.tip: Two years of continuous officiating or temporary service, waived for SC/ST temporary or officiating officers.

quote.text: Officers with a continuous officiating or temporary service of two years or more, will be granted in addition to any leave which they are eligible for, leave under this rule for obtaining superior qualifications
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 91 Superior qualifications

facts.prompt: Is Rule 91 leave given for broken periods?
facts.tip: No, it covers the entire period of the course; extension is given in case of failure.

quote.text: Such leave will not, however be given for broken periods but will cover the entire period of the course concerned.

facts.prompt: What service is needed for post-graduate course leave under Rule 91A?
facts.tip: Continuous officiating or temporary service of 5 years or more.

quote.text: Officers with a continuous officiating or temporary service of 5 years or more may be granted in addition to any leave to which they are eligible for, leave for undergoing Post-graduate Courses
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 91A Post-graduate courses

facts.prompt: Who can sanction leave under Rule 91 and study leave under Rule 99?
facts.tip: Rule 91 leave: authority sanctioning eligible leave and LWA. Study leave under Rule 99: only Government.

quote.text: Leave under this rule can be sanctioned by the authority competent to sanction eligible leave and leave without allowances. Study leave under Rule 99, Part I, can be sanctioned only by Government.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 91 Government Decision

facts.prompt: Special allowance for officiating in a second post with full charge of own
facts.tip: It must not exceed 6 per cent of the minimum of the scale of pay of the other post.

quote.text: special allowance which should not exceed * 6 per cent of the minimum of the scale of pay of other post
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 53(b)(1) Combination of appointments

facts.prompt: Special allowance for current duties only of additional post
facts.tip: It must not exceed 3 per cent of the minimum of the scale of pay of that post.

quote.text: should not exceed *3 per cent of the minimum of the scale of pay of that post

facts.prompt: When is special allowance for additional charge allowed?
facts.tip: Only if the additional charge exceeds 14 working days (full charge) or one month (current duties only).

quote.text: unless the period of additional charge exceeds fourteen working days in the case of full additional charge and one month in the case of discharge of current duties only.

facts.prompt: Maximum period of special allowance for additional charge
facts.tip: Special allowance for additional charge must not be allowed for more than three months on any account.

quote.text: should not be allowed for a period exceeding three months on any account.

facts.prompt: What is the maximum casual leave in a calendar year?
facts.tip: 20 days; teaching staff of educational institutions 15 days.

quote.text: No officer may in any case be absent on casual leave for more than twenty days in the course of one calendar year. But the members of the teaching staff of educational institutions shall be eligible for casual leave only for fifteen days in a calendar year.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Appendix VII para 2(i) Casual leave

facts.prompt: What is the maximum absence combining casual leave with holidays?
facts.tip: Resulting absence must not exceed fifteen days at a stretch.

quote.text: provided that the resulting period of absence from duty shall not exceed fifteen days at a stretch.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Appendix VII para 2(ii)

facts.prompt: Can casual leave be retrospectively commuted into other leave?
facts.tip: No, as it is not recognised as leave.

quote.text: Casual leave, not being recognised as leave, cannot be retrospectively commuted into any other kind of leave
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Appendix VII para 7

facts.prompt: When is an honorarium sanctioned?
facts.tip: An honorarium should not be sanctioned unless the work had prior Government consent and its amount was settled in advance, except for recorded special reasons.

quote.text: sanction to the grant or acceptance of an honorarium should not be given unless the work has been undertaken with the prior consent of the Government and its amount has been settled in advance.

facts.prompt: How much of a large fee goes to General Revenues?
facts.tip: One-third of a non-recurring fee over Rs 2000 or a recurring fee over Rs 1250 a year is credited to General Revenues.

quote.text: one-third of any non-recurring fee exceeding # ` 2000 or one-third of any recurring fee exceeding # ` 1250 a year, paid to an officer, shall be credited to the General Revenues.

facts.prompt: Can an officer do outside work for fees freely?
facts.tip: No officer may do work for another Government or private body or accept a fee without Government sanction.

quote.text: No officer may undertake work for another Government, or a private or public body or a private person, or accept fee therefore, without the sanction of the Government.

facts.prompt: What happens to leave with allowances when an officer is suspended while on it?
facts.tip: Suspension cancels the leave for the period of suspension, and he gets subsistence allowance.

quote.text: In the case of an Officer on leave with allowances, the orders of suspension shall have the effect of cancelling the leave for the period of suspension. He shall be entitled to subsistence allowance.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 55B(ii) Suspension during leave

facts.prompt: What if an officer is suspended while on leave without allowances?
facts.tip: No subsistence allowance during the leave; it is payable on expiry if suspension continues.

quote.text: he shall not be eligible for any subsistence allowance during the period of the leave. On the expiry of the leave if he continues to be on suspension, he shall be entitled to the subsistence allowance.

facts.prompt: On which form is leave applied for?
facts.tip: Form No. 13, to the authority competent to grant it.

quote.text: An application for leave or an extension of leave must be made to the authority competent to grant such leave or extension in Form No. 13.
quote.ref: KSR Part I, Rule 113 Application for leave

facts.prompt: Who maintains the leave account of gazetted and non-gazetted officers?
facts.tip: Audit Officer for gazetted officers; Head of Office for non-gazetted officers.

quote.text: Leave account of a Gazetted Officer will be maintained by the Audit Officer. The leave account of a non-gazetted officer will be maintained by the Head of the Office in which he is employed.

facts.prompt: Who can relax KSR rules in undue hardship?
facts.tip: Government, if satisfied that a rule causes undue hardship, may dispense with or relax it.

quote.text: Where Government are satisfied that the operation of any rule under these rules causes undue hardship in any particular case, the Government may dispense with or relax the requirements of that rule

facts.prompt: Who decides if KSR applies to a person in doubt?
facts.tip: The matter is referred to Government and its decision is final.

quote.text: If any doubt arises as to whether these rules apply to any person, the matter shall be referred to the Government and the decision of the Government shall be final.

facts.prompt: What happens on substantive appointment to a permanent post?
facts.tip: The officer acquires a lien on that post and ceases to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post.

quote.text: an officer on substantive appointment to any permanent post acquires a lien on that post and ceases to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post.

facts.prompt: Can a lien be terminated with the officer's consent?
facts.tip: No. A lien cannot be terminated, even with consent, if he is left with no lien or suspended lien on a permanent post.

quote.text: An officer’s lien on a post may in no circumstances be terminated, even with his consent, if the result will be to leave him without a lien or a suspended lien upon a permanent post.

facts.prompt: Can an officer be transferred to a lower-paid post?
facts.tip: Except for inefficiency or misbehaviour, or on his written request, an officer shall not be transferred substantively to a post carrying less pay.

quote.text: except- (1) on account of inefficiency or misbehavior, or (2) on his written request, an officer shall not be transferred substantively to, or except in a case covered by Rule 58, appointed to officiate in a post carrying less pay than the pay of the permanent post

facts.prompt: What is a transfer?
facts.tip: A transfer is movement of an officer from one headquarter station to another to take up a new post or due to change of headquarters.

quote.text: Transfer.- means the movement of an officer from one headquarter station in which he is employed to another such station

facts.prompt: Reinstated after full exoneration: what pay?
facts.tip: He is paid full pay and allowances as if not dismissed, removed, compulsorily retired or suspended.

quote.text: the officer shall, subject to the provisions of sub-rule (6) be paid the full pay and allowances to which he would have been entitled had he not been dismissed, removed or compulsorily retired or suspended

facts.prompt: Time limit on payment on reinstatement (Rule 56(4))
facts.tip: Payment is restricted to three years immediately preceding reinstatement or retirement on superannuation.

quote.text: any payment under this sub-rule shall be restricted to a period of three years immediately preceding reinstatement or retirement on superannuation

facts.prompt: To whom is a superannuation pension granted?
facts.tip: It is granted to an officer entitled or compelled, by rule, to retire at a particular age.

quote.text: A superannuation pension is granted to an officer entitled or compelled, by rule, to retire at a particular age.
quote.ref: KSR Part III, Rule 55 Superannuation Pension

facts.prompt: To whom is invalid pension granted?
facts.tip: To an employee certified by a Medical Board or Medical Officer to be permanently incapacitated for the public service or the particular branch he belongs to.

quote.text: is certified by such Medical Board or Medical Officer to be permanently incapacitated by a contagious disease or physical or mental disability or infirmity for the public service
quote.ref: KSR Part III, Rule 42(2) Invalid Pension

facts.prompt: What is the limit on compassionate allowance to a dismissed employee?
facts.tip: It must not exceed two-thirds of the pension admissible had he retired on the date of dismissal or removal.

quote.text: the allowances granted to any employee shall not exceed two-thirds of the pension which would have been admissible to him if he had retired on the date of dismissal or removal.

facts.prompt: How early must a pension application be submitted?
facts.tip: At least one year in advance of the anticipated date of retirement, in Form 11.

quote.text: Every government employee should submit his formal application for pension at least one year in advance of the date of his anticipated retirement:

facts.prompt: Can an employee retire in order to be re-employed and draw pension with pay?
facts.tip: No. An employee may not retire with a view to being re-employed and drawing pension in addition to pay.

quote.text: An employee may not retire with the view to being re-employed, and drawing pension in addition to pay
